Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking our RFP. Our security review team has a few focused asks so we can complete the vendor short-list: a concise network segmentation diagram showing control plane vs. customer data plane boundaries, a matrix mapping data flows (ingress/egress) with classification (PII/PHI/other), and a short attack-surface summary that highlights how Redwood's private deployment option minimizes lateral movement risk.

Specific questions we need answered by EOD Aug 18:
- Which components sit in customer VPC vs. Redwood-managed control plane?
- How are secrets and model keys stored (KMS/HSM)?
- What network-level controls enforce isolation (security groups, AZ/region segmentation, private interconnects)?
- Example failover paths and how fallbacks affect data locality and audit logging.

If you can send a diagram (PNG) and a short one-page threat summary + an isolation matrix spreadsheet that maps flows to controls, that would be ideal.

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear asks. We're happy to provide the artifacts you requested.

Quick summary (details & attachments follow):
- Control plane: hosted by Redwood (separate VPCs per region, dedicated control-plane subnet). No customer data stored in control-plane replicas.
- Customer data plane: runs in the customer-managed VPC for Private deployments (VPC peering / PrivateLink for on-cloud installs) or in a logically separated dedicated tenant pool for Dedicated offering.
- Secrets: customer-managed KMS supported for Private; Redwood-managed KMS with HSM-backed keys for Dedicated/Hosted (customer key import available).
- Network enforcement: security groups + NACLs, mandatory mutual TLS between runtime and backend, and route-level policies to prevent transitive access across tenant pools.

I've attached a compact diagram and an isolation matrix that maps the most common ingress/egress flows and the controls we apply. Also attaching our updated isolation whitepaper for reference.

Proposed next step: a 45-minute deep-dive with our architecture team (Karthik + Neha) the week of Aug 19 to walk through the diagram and answer technical questions. Does Aug 19 or Aug 20 work for your team?

Thanks,

Jordan / Neha — looping in a few technical clarifications before we send the final files to Atlas. I pasted the short threat-summary text and the diagram legend below for review. If we're aligned I'll send the annotated PNG + matrix as-is.

--- excerpt to include in customer brief ---
Executive attack-surface summary (high level):
- Control plane compromise: control plane components are isolated in separate AWS accounts/VPCs with strict IAM and least-privilege for orchestration services. No long-term customer model data or request payloads are retained in the control plane.
- Data plane lateral movement: customer workloads run in isolated tenant pools; we apply process-level sandboxing, mandatory mutual TLS, and per-tenant network policies. KV caches are scoped per-request and are destroyed after session TTL.
- Key exposure risk: keys are stored in HSM-backed KMS; customer-managed keys (BYOK) are recommended for regulated workloads. Access to KMS requires per-call auth with short-lived tokens and is logged with request IDs for audit.
- Fallback modes: when routing to a lower-cost variant or fallback model, request bodies are still processed within the same tenant boundary; only model artifact selection changes. We emit a model-selection event to the audit log for traceability.

Diagram legend (for PNG):
1) Customer VPC (Private deployment): inference runtime nodes, customer data stores.
2) Redwood control plane: deployment manager, image registry, rollout controller (no customer payloads).
3) Network enforcement: private interconnect, security groups, mTLS gateways, and restricted egress proxies.

Small edit suggested: change wording in the second paragraph of the summary from \"no customer data stored in control plane\" to \"no customer payloads persist in the control plane; metadata for orchestration is ephemeral and audited\".

If that wording is OK I will finalize the PNG and XLSX.

-Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

What we attached:

- redwood_isolation_whitepaper_v2.pdf (detailed deployment patterns & HSM/KMS options)

Short operational notes:
- Private deployment mode: control plane is operated by Redwood but the inference runtime that processes customer payloads can be deployed in your VPC. All inter-service traffic is mutual-TLS and routes are explicitly whitelisted; no cross-tenant routing is permitted.
- For Dedicated customers: we provision tenant pools with network ACLs and enforced egress through Redwood-managed egress proxies to satisfy policy.
- Key management: we support BYOK (customer-imported HSM keys) for highest assurance; default is HSM-backed Redwood KMS with full audit trails forwarded to customer SIEM on request.

Next step: we propose a 45-minute technical deep-dive on Aug 19 (10:00-10:45 PDT) with Karthik and Neha to walk through the diagram and answer any control-specific questions. Confirm and we'll send a calendar invite + a short runbook.
